name: IntuneFirewallMigration
description: IntuneFirewallMigration is a public-preview tool that migrates Group Policy and local firewall rules into Intune as Settings Catalog policies. It supports selecting specific firewall profiles (Domain, Private, Public) and importing only inbound or outbound rules, using Microsoft.Graph.Authentication with Invoke-MgGraphRequest. The script disables telemetry, requires Graph permissions (DeviceManagementConfiguration.ReadWrite.All), and works with PowerShell 5 or 7 to modernize firewall management in Intune.
keywords: how to migrate firewall rules to intune
author: Nick Benton

securityCheck.aiSummary: The codebase appears to be a legitimate Intune firewall migration tool with Graph integration and proper authentication flows overall. The most notable security concerns are a packaging misconfiguration in the module manifest (RootModule mismatch) that could block or redirect module loading, and the use of a command-line appSecret parameter which risks secret exposure. No obfuscated code, no data exfiltration, and no evident malicious behavior were detected. Recommended mitigations: fix the manifest RootModule to point to the correct file, review Private/Strings.ps1 for integrity, and adopt vault/cert-based authentication instead of passing app secrets on the command line. Ensure PSGallery module installation is signed and trusted to reduce supply-chain risk.

noMaliciousPatterns.reason: Module manifest RootModule points to 'IntuneFirewallRuleMigration.psm1' while the repository contains 'IntuneFirewallMigration.psm1'. This packaging misconfiguration could prevent the module from loading and executing as intended. If an attacker or a misbuild redirects tooling, it could introduce risk. Action: correct RootModule to the actual root module file and validate module import paths.
